scope: Local registered FastMCP validation path; capture callback replaces retrieval. No deployed or clinical validation.

tools.name: route_parent_question
tools.description:
Call FIRST for parent-facing requests, before evidence retrieval. Returns fixed
referral/urgent/identity/privacy guidance and allow_research. If false, show the
message with source URLs and stop research. Rule-based prototype, NOT validated
clinical triage. Country is explicit; never invent a local emergency number.
Do not include names, contact details, birth dates or medical record numbers.

tools.name: get_parent_medication_info
tools.description:
Preferred for parent questions about side effects and breastfeeding infant findings.
Use this focused bundle, not medication_safety_brief, when papers/trials/FAERS
are not requested. Parent-facing evidence bundle after confirming drug identity. Separates label
adverse effects in the medicine taker, LactMed infant evidence, and MedlinePlus
education links. Monitoring recommendations are not observed infant effects.
Follow source limitations; never diagnose symptoms or give personal medication
decisions, doses, schedules, missed-dose or taper instructions.

tools.name: search_medication_recalls
tools.description:
FDA drug enforcement recall candidates, including historical records. Show
manufacturer, product/formulation text, lots, dates, status and reason. A literal
lot mention is NOT confirmation; ranges and all-lot notices need verification.
Never clear a bottle from absent/different lot results. Consumer instructions
may be missing: refer to official notice/pharmacist, never invent them.

tools.name: search_drug_safety_alerts
tools.description:
Search titles on the current FDA Drug Safety Communications index. Returns
dates and official notice links, not full notices, personal advice or all archives.
No match does not establish safety; use exact brand/generic words separately.

tools.name: find_recruiting_studies
tools.description:
Preferred for participation questions ("can I join a study?"). Use search_trials
for a research landscape across statuses, not enrollment discovery.
Discover potentially relevant RECRUITING studies and public eligibility,
contacts, site status, locations and update dates. Location is city/state/country,
not home address. Not an eligibility decision or enrollment. Overall recruitment
does not mean every site recruits; study team must confirm current availability.
Use population='pediatric' for children: only records with pediatric age metadata
are listed; adult-only and unverified-age records are withheld. If none remain,
lead with no verified pediatric match in this bounded search, not broader studies.

tools.name: search_pregnancy_registries
tools.description:
FDA-listed pregnancy exposure registries: medicine/condition, registry, public
contacts, source status and links. FDA does not run or endorse them; list is not
comprehensive. Verify enrollment with registry. No eligibility or safety claim.

tools.name: search_parent_input_opportunities
tools.description:
Discover NIH/FDA Federal Register notices plus public-engagement directories.
Use a concise subject such as 'clinical research' or 'pregnancy', not a whole
question or extra words such as 'parent public input'. If empty, simplify the
subject while preserving the research topic; do not invent opportunities.
Candidates may be RFIs, comment requests or meetings; verify title/text, audience,
official deadline and submission instructions. Use comment_deadline.date and
relation_to_as_of to group dates, separately from submission_status and relevance.
A known future date is not an unknown date even if submission acceptance is
unverified. Meeting dates never establish comment deadlines or closure.
Unknown comment deadline is neither verified open nor verified closed.
Coverage is incomplete. Never submit comments or collect personal histories.

tools.name: get_reporting_resources
tools.description:
Official navigation links for FDA MedWatch and NIH/FDA public involvement.
No report/comment submitted. Reporting does not prove causation or replace urgent
care. Do not collect identifiable medical details in this MCP.

tools.name: normalize_drug
tools.description:
Resolve a brand name, misspelling or combination product to standard generic
ingredient(s) and an RxNorm ID (RxNorm, NLM). Call this first when unsure of the drug name.
found=false means unverified. requires_confirmation=true means a tentative match:
ask for confirmation; never silently substitute its ingredient as the intended drug.

tools.name: search_lactmed
tools.description:
Find LactMed (Drugs and Lactation Database, NLM) records by drug name.
Returns IDs to pass to get_lactmed_record.

tools.name: get_lactmed_record

book_id.description: Numeric id returned by search_lactmed; not an NBK accession or drug name.
book_id.title: Book Id

tools.description:
Get LactMed text for one record: use during lactation, drug levels, effects on
breastfed infants and on lactation, alternatives. First call search_lactmed and pass
its numeric id as book_id. Never pass a drug name or invent a record ID.
Separate measured exposure, observed infant outcomes, and source recommendations.
A recommendation to monitor a symptom is NOT evidence that the symptom occurred.
Preserve separate case-report events and timing: do not merge exposure changes
with outcome observations, infer unstated timing, or imply proven causation.
Include only relevant supported details; explicitly identify unspecified timing.
For partial chronology, group only explicitly linked events rather than a fully
ordered sequence; name the specific ordering that remains unknown.
If outcome text is truncated, retrieve more with max_chars (up to 20000) or
state the limitation; do not infer outcomes from monitoring advice.

tools.name: semantic_search_lactmed
tools.description:
Natural-language search over LactMed (e.g. 'antidepressants safe for a newborn').
Requires the Vector Search index; otherwise explains how to fall back.

tools.name: search_literature
tools.description:
Search PubMed literature. 'keyword' hits live PubMed (MeSH-filtered by population);
'semantic' uses the lakehouse vector index of maternal/child abstracts; 'auto' prefers semantic.
Use a concise query (drug plus one concept), not a whole question. If empty, simplify
without dropping the drug. Check relevance and call get_abstracts before describing
study findings. Empty results do not establish absence of evidence.

tools.name: get_abstracts

items.description: Exact numeric PMID from a returned PubMed record.

tools.description:
Get abstracts and canonical PubMed source URLs for up to 10 PubMed IDs.
Cite each article's returned URL. No returned article is a retrieval limitation,
not evidence that a paper or research does not exist.

tools.name: get_label_sections
tools.description:
FDA label (via DailyMed, NLM) pregnancy, lactation and pediatric-use sections.
OTC labels may return pregnancy_lactation as one combined warning.
Identify the returned product title; do not generalize across formulations.
Report returned source warnings and missing_standalone_sections. A combined
warning does not provide pediatric-use evidence. Missing sections are retrieval limitations;
do not fill them with uncited medical claims or infer safety.

tools.name: search_pediatric_labeling_changes
tools.description:
Search FDA historical pediatric labeling changes by generic or trade name.
Returns dates, product/indication scope, BPCA/PREA category and FDA summaries.
BPCA/PREA filters include rows listing both. Match names, not full questions;
try generic or brand separately if no match. Preserve age, indication and
formulation limits in source text. A labeling change is not automatically an
approval or proof of safety. BPCA designation does not imply NIH funding.
Cite the FDA source and workbook row; do not turn historical dose text into
dosing advice. Use get_label_sections separately for current product labeling.
Empty results do not establish absence of pediatric evidence.

tools.name: search_trials
tools.description:
Research landscape across trial statuses, including historical studies.
For joining a study, location, contacts or current enrollment, prefer
find_recruiting_studies. Search ClinicalTrials.gov for pregnancy, lactation or pediatrics.
Use returned conditions, interventions and summaries to assess relevance. Omit
indirect matches from the main answer; registration/status is not evidence of benefit.
When asked to omit dose numbers, use intervention name_without_strength.
It is display formatting, not normalized ingredient identity; original name is retained.
Link EVERY listed study using its returned study URL and state its exact status.
For current/ongoing studies, separate RECRUITING, ENROLLING_BY_INVITATION and
ACTIVE_NOT_RECRUITING from NOT_YET_RECRUITING, historical/closed and UNKNOWN.
ACTIVE_NOT_RECRUITING does not mean open enrollment. Never place completed or
unknown-status studies in the ongoing list. State when no relevant ongoing study
was returned; do not imply the search was exhaustive.

tools.name: search_funded_research
tools.description:
Search NIH RePORTER for funded projects (newest first) on a maternal/child topic.
Use title and abstract to assess relevance; omit indirect matches from the main
answer. A funded project is not a completed finding or proof of MPRINT membership.

tools.name: search_mprint_gold

anyOf.description: Exact numeric PMID from a returned PubMed record.

tools.description:
Search a versioned snapshot of MPRINT Gold expert-curated study metadata by
drug name or exact PMID. For a Gold record by PMID, pass pmid and omit drug.
If both are supplied, both must match. Never substitute automated Silver
classifications when Gold is requested. Returns PMID links, population,
study type and source row provenance.
This is actual published MPRINT Gold data, not MPRINT keyword matching.
Optional filters conservatively match source population and study-type labels.
Resolve verified brand names to ingredient names via RxNorm; ambiguous matches
require confirmation. Do not equate RxCUIs with MPRINT UMLS CUIs.
This search returns study metadata; use get_mprint_gold_outcomes for aggregate
curated outcomes by PMID. Report the snapshot date and any result limits.
Inclusion does not prove safety, efficacy, quality or MPRINT funding. Retrieve
abstracts/full papers before summarizing outcomes. Empty matches may reflect
limited snapshot coverage or a synonym; never infer an evidence gap from absence.

tools.name: get_mprint_gold_outcomes

pmid.description: Exact numeric PMID from a returned PubMed record.
pmid.title: Pmid

offset.description: Row offset from next_offset in the preceding result.
offset.title: Offset

tools.description:
Retrieve curated aggregate MPRINT Gold outcome rows for one PubMed ID.
Preserves source values, units, statistics, uncertainty and notes. PE/CT and
PK-summary tables only; individual-patient rows and PK parameters excluded.
Context links use PMID AND curation workbook/folder, not cohort/arm matching.
These linkage rules are MCP implementation guidance, not dataset-author claims.
Never attribute every outcome to every drug in the paper. Null means missing
in the exported data, not zero or proof the original paper did not report it.
Say "missing in the exported data" for null fields.
Check source exposure/population, denominators and intervals before
interpreting. Use next_offset to page; disclose limits and snapshot age.
Cite the paper and dataset row; consult the original paper for missing context.
Do not turn historical doses or observed associations into treatment advice.

tools.name: get_mprint_silver_classifications

items.description: Exact numeric PMID from a returned PubMed record.

tools.description:
Look up up to 20 PubMed IDs in the published MPRINT Silver study-type snapshot.
Returns automated PK/PE/CT labels and source rows, not clinical conclusions.
Use PMIDs from PubMed or Gold; do not invent identifiers. Silver drug/population
mappings are NOT loaded. Distinguish automated Silver labels from curated Gold.
No match does not mean the paper is irrelevant or that no research exists.

tools.name: search_mprint
tools.description:
Maternal and Pediatric Precision in Therapeutics (MPRINT) Hub (NICHD) related work.
No public MPRINT API is confirmed; this searches NIH RePORTER and PubMed for MPRINT-related
records. For direct published Gold metadata use search_mprint_gold; for Silver
study-type labels by PMID use get_mprint_silver_classifications.

tools.name: get_adverse_event_signals
tools.description:
Most frequently reported reactions in FDA FAERS (openFDA) for a drug, optionally for
pregnancy-exposure or infant reports. Counts are spontaneous reports, NOT incidence or proof of causation.

tools.name: get_patient_education

anyOf.description: RxNorm concept identifier, not a drug name.

tools.description: Plain-language information from MedlinePlus (NLM) for a health topic or, with an RxNorm ID, a drug.

tools.name: search_bpca_evidence
tools.description: Discover NICHD BPCA/PTN study-summary links by drug/title words. Returns index titles and links, NOT PDF contents or clinical conclusions. Empty query lists summaries.

tools.name: search_nichd_studies
tools.description: Search public NICHD DASH study descriptions and publications, optionally MFMU or Neonatal Research Network. Zero-based pages. Controlled underlying datasets are NOT retrieved; access process is required.

tools.name: medication_safety_brief
tools.description:
Broad cross-source research brief when papers, trials or reporting signals are requested.
Prefer get_parent_medication_info for focused parent side-effect/infant questions;
prefer find_recruiting_studies for participation. This is not a personal safety verdict.
Combination products cover only the first ingredient, with an explicit warning.
Pediatric FAERS coverage here is infant-only, not all pediatric age groups.
One-call evidence brief for a medication in pregnancy, lactation or pediatrics:
resolves the name (RxNorm), then gathers LactMed, FDA label sections, recent literature,
adverse-event signals, trial records and plain-language MedlinePlus info, with citations.
